text: The answer must be in the text, but it cannot be written word for word.
The library closes at nine, so students can’t be there at ten.
The group rooms are booked online, so there must be a booking website.
She left the last three questions blank. She must have run out of time.
He changed his answer. He might have had a hunch, or he may have found proof.
The answer must be supported by the text, even if it is not written word for word.
That option repeats the words of the passage, so it could be a distractor.
She left three questions blank, so she must have run out of time.
He finished in ten minutes, so he cannot have read the whole passage.
I will not change my answer unless a line in the text proves it wrong.

The students who read the most are often the slowest on the reading section, and I think I know why. They were trained to find the answer in the text. They see a question, go back to the passage, and look for the sentence that says it. On an inference question, that sentence does not exist. The text gives you two facts, and the answer is what must be true if both facts are true. So here is the exercise I give everyone. Before you look at the options, answer the question in your own words. If your answer is something the text could not possibly support, you are guessing. If it follows from two sentences, you have made an inference. Then look at the options, and choose the one that says your answer in different words.

Good morning, everyone. A few changes at the law library this week. Because of the exam period, the second floor is now reserved for silent study, and phones must be switched off before you go up the stairs. The group rooms on the first floor are in high demand, so they can only be booked online, for a maximum of two hours. If you booked a room last week by email, please book it again on the website, because those requests were not saved. On Friday the library closes at six instead of ten, for maintenance. And finally, the printer on the ground floor is not working. The one on the first floor is.
The group rooms are booked online, so there must be a booking website.
The library closes at nine, so students cannot be inside at ten.
She left three questions blank, so she must have run out of time.
I am not sure why he changed it. He might have had a hunch.
Read quickly for the general idea: skim the passage first.
Remove the options the text does not support: eliminate them.
